title: Multimodal Assessment of Recovery Trajectories after Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (allo-HSCT)
summary:
This research project examines the recovery process following an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-HSCT). In this procedure, patients receive blood-forming stem cells from another person (a donor). This treatment is used for certain severe blood disorders.  

The first 100 days after transplantation are particularly important. During this time, the immune system is often severely weakened (immunosuppression). This leads to an increased risk of infections and other transplant-related complications. In addition, changes in blood counts may occur (including cytopenias, i.e., a deficiency of certain blood cells).  

Many patients also experience psychological and physical stress during this phase, such as severe fatigue, sleep disturbances, mood swings, or difficulties with concentration and memory. Although it is well known that the first 100 days after a transplant are a particularly critical phase, there have been few studies to date that examine the course of physical and psychological recovery during this period and enable predictions about the further course of recovery.  

In this study, we aim to support patients undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation at the University Hospital RWTH Aachen. Participants in this study will be followed for a period of 12 months starting on the day of transplantation (Day 0). During this time, we will regularly collect various data regarding your health status and recovery process.  

Some of the data will be collected through brief surveys using the two scientifically validated smartphone apps developed by the Jülich Research Center—“JTrack Social” and “JTrack EMA.” These so-called “flash surveys” consist of 10 short questions about your current well-being and are administered every two days.  The JTrack Social app enables passive data collection, which takes place automatically without any active input. For example, it records information about movement, activity patterns, or smartphone usage. The content of messages, conversations, or personal files is not recorded. Through the “JTrack EMA” app, you’ll be asked nine short questions every two days, including questions about sleep quality, mood, and distressing thoughts. 

In addition, participants are asked to fill out questionnaires (covering topics such as mood, specific thoughts, psychological stress, sleep quality, pain, and physical symptoms) on paper approximately every 2 to 4 weeks. We also use this app to collect data automatically without requiring active input. For example, information about physical activity, activity patterns, or smartphone usage is recorded. The content of messages, conversations, or personal files is not collected.  

We also use the results of routine clinical examinations that are conducted as part of your treatment anyway. These include blood and laboratory test results that provide indications of how the immune system is rebuilding itself after the transplant (immune regeneration). Participants will not be required to undergo any additional blood draws or medical examinations as part of our study.
conditions: hematologic disorders that meet the criteria for allogeneic stem cell transplantation
Malignant neoplasms, stated or presumed to be primary, of lymphoid, haematopoietic and related tissue
Immunodeficiency associated with other major defects

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients with a confirmed indication for allogeneic HSCT will be recruited. Inclusion will occur after comprehensive oral and written information about the study and the option to withdraw at any time, and following written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not have a confirmed indication for allogeneic HSCT will not be included in the study. In addition, patients who do have a confirmed indication for allogeneic HSCT but but for whom, due to severe somatic or psychiatric limitations, the psychological and medical teams have jointly determined that performing an allogeneic HSCT is not justifiable (e.g., paranoid schizophrenia with noncompliance regarding medication).
